input.question: What makes banks special enough to be able to hold electronic money? What is stopping people from just opening their own accounts?
input.ground_truth: Banks are tightly regulated by the government, required to follow thousands of laws and rules, and subject to constant inspection and detailed audits at any time. Therefore they are trusted to manage certain financial tasks.

Explain the following question in a simple way as if you are explaining to a 5-year-old.

Question: What makes banks special enough to be able to hold electronic money? What is stopping people from just opening their own accounts?

Answer:

response.prediction:
Okay, let’s imagine a toy box.

A bank is like a big, super-safe toy box that everyone trusts. You can put your toy coins (which are like your electronic money) inside, and you know they’ll be safe. If you want to give your toys to a friend, you just tell the toy box helper (the bank), and they help you give the toys to your friend without you having to carry them all the way there.

Now, why can’t you just make your own toy box at home? Well, everyone has to trust your toy box to keep their toys safe. If you just make a box in your room, your friends might not believe it’s as safe as the big toy box that lots of people use. Also, the big toy box (the bank) has special rules and helpers to make sure no one steals the toys and to make sure everyone plays fair.

So, banks are special because everyone trusts them to keep money safe and help move it around easily. That’s why we use banks instead of making our own little boxes at home!
